IB Revision Courses FAQ
About the course
There are two pre-IB maths courses, one for current Year 11 students wishing to study SL or HL Analysis and Approaches and one for current Year 11 students wishing to study SL or HL Applications and Interpretations. Both will cover similar material; however, the mathematical approach will differ depending on the course. Students are advised to have a GDC to help them best prepare and get the most out of these courses.
These courses are not aimed at students who have already completed an Additional Maths course.
Classes start at 09:00 on each course day and conclude at 16:15 on the first day of the course. There is an hour for lunch (provided as part of the cost) in the middle of each day, as well as morning and afternoon breaks.
The syllabus of the Pre-IB Maths Analysis Course and the Pre-IB Maths Applications covers similar topics. However, the teaching and learning approach is different.
You should choose one 3-day Pre-IB Maths Analysis Course OR one 3-day Pre-IB Maths Applications Course.
Pre-IB Maths course topics
course dates

Boarders arrive on the evening of Saturday 22 August between 16:00-19:00, and depart at 16:30 on Tuesday 25 August.
Wednesday 26 August - Friday 28 August
Boarders arrive on the evening of Tuesday 25 August between 16:00-19:00, and depart at 16:30 on Friday 28 August.
Use of School Facilities
Whether as a residential or day student, those attending the course(s) will have access to some of the school’s outstanding facilities, including the athletics track, tennis nets, five-a-side football pitches , volleyball and basketball courts. There is a wide expanse of school playing fields on the main school campus.
The Non-residential Option
Those who live, or can find accommodation, close enough to the school to enable them to attend a course on a non-residential basis may prefer to do so. They will also be given morning and afternoon refreshments, and lunch.
The Residential Option
Those attending either residential course will be asked to arrive at their allocated residence any time between 16:00 and 19:00 on the day before the course starts and will stay a total of three nights for each course. Students will be accommodated in one of the school’s boarding houses. All residents will be accommodated in single or twin bedrooms where there will be facilities to study in the evening. A member of the school’s academic boarding staff will be on duty during the course and be responsible for residents. Breakfast, morning and afternoon refreshments, lunch and an evening meal will be provided in the school’s central dining room.
Please note that it may be necessary for students to share accommodation although, if a single is requested, these will be offered on a ‘first come, first served’ basis.

IB Revision Courses
Every year, our IB revision and review courses offer outstanding and reliable assistance to students. The revision courses support those revising for their IB Diploma exams, while the review courses provide a structured review of the content and skills covered during the first year of IB Diploma studies. We also offer a pre-IB Maths course for Year 11 students who will be embarking on the IB Mathematics courses.
“The lessons were amazing, I found the courses really interesting and useful, and I learnt a lot from the teachers about exam technique.”
IB courses overview
Easter Revision Courses
Pre-IB Summer Maths Revision Courses
Mid-IB Summer Review Courses
IB Revision Courses FAQ
About the courses
Easter IB Revision Courses
Easter IB revision courses held in April are suitable for students in their final year of the IB Diploma Programme, and are intended as intensive exam preparation revision courses.
Applications are open from October 2025.
Pre-IB Summer Maths Revision Courses
Our Pre-IB Maths revision courses held in August are aimed at Year 11 students who will be embarking on the IB Higher Level or the Standard Level course in Mathematics without having studied Maths beyond IGCSE or GCSE or equivalent.
Applications are open from January 2026.
Mid-IB Summer Review Courses
Our Mid-IB summer review courses take place in August and are aimed at students who have just completed their first year of the IB Diploma Programme, and would like to consolidate their learning before they move forward to the final year.
Applications are open from January 2026.
Sevenoaks and the IB
Sevenoaks has been teaching and administering the IB since the 1970s, with over 400 students on the IB Diploma Programme every year. The school can draw on a wealth of experience from teaching staff who are fully familiar with the syllabuses and the academic standards required to achieve success in the IB Diploma.
Unsurprisingly, therefore, we are confident that those joining our revision courses will receive the very best teaching and preparation for their IB exams.
Our Teaching Approach
Our courses are both for those students looking to assure themselves of the top grades and for students who are struggling with the IB.
Where possible, classes are setted. Our teachers ensure students are fully aware of the necessary ground to cover to be successful in the final exams, focussing on the core content of courses. Students receive intensive tuition in their chosen subject with a carefully structured and organised schedule supported by suitable written and visual resources to help prepare for exams.
Our teachers seek to enter a dialogue with students over what topics or skills they wish to focus on, and take this into account, while still aiming to cover as much of the core course as possible.
Our teachers help students improve their exam techniques to ensure they develop the necessary skills to answer IB exam questions successfully. Students will receive advice on how best to revise for their forthcoming exams.
Teaching is conducted in groups of 10 students or fewer at the school, in comfortable well-equipped classrooms. Our courses are taken by both Sevenoaks students and external students alike, with students arriving from all over the world.
“Thank you for all the resources, they have proven to be extremely useful and I will definitely be using them for the rest of my revision. ”

About the courses
The Easter IB Revision Courses are suitable for students who are coming to the end of their study for their IB Diploma and are about to take their exams in May (ie Upper Sixth or Year 13 students). The purpose of these courses is to provide students with a carefully structured and organised intensive 17.5 hours (over three days) of revision as they prepare for their final examinations.
Teaching will be conducted in small groups in the school, in comfortable well-equipped classrooms.
In this time the teachers, many of whom are or have been employed full-time at Sevenoaks School, will:
The Structure and Range of the Revision Courses
Applicants are invited to apply for either one or two courses. Each course will include a total of 17.5 hours tuition and teaching over three days. Classes start at 09.00 and conclude at 16.30 for the two full days and finish at 16.00 on the final day. With an hour for lunch (provided as part of the cost) in the middle of the day, the morning and afternoon sessions are intensive. Students are also expected to complete approximately two hours of work on the two evenings when there are classes the following day.

Whether as a residential or day student, those attending a review course will have access to the school’s outstanding facilities, including the sports centre. For fresh air and exercise there is the wide expanse of school playing fields adjoining the main school campus.
The Residential Option
Those attending either or both courses will be asked to arrive at their allocated residence any time between 16:00 and 19:00 on the night before the day the course starts and will stay a total of three nights for each course. Students will be accommodated in one of the school’s boarding houses. All residents will be accommodated in single or twin bed-sitting rooms where there will be facilities to study in the evening. A member of the school’s academic boarding house staff will be on duty during the course and be responsible for residents. Breakfast, morning and afternoon refreshments, lunch and an evening meal will be provided in the school’s central dining room.
Please note that it may be necessary for students to share accommodation although, if a single is requested, these will be offered on a ‘first come, first served’ basis.
The Non-residential Option
Those who live, or can find accommodation, close enough to the school to enable them to attend a course on a non-residential basis may prefer to do so. They will also be given morning and afternoon refreshments, and lunch. Please bear in mind that the residential option means living in a boarding house and abiding by the rules of the boarding house. Academic IB Revision Courses
IB Revision Courses FAQ
What should I bring?
Bring any notes you may have been given or taken on the subject in the last 18 months (for the Easter course and Maths course) or the last 12 months (for the Summer course), as well as writing implements, rulers, calculators etc. If you wish to make use of the Sennocke Centre, then please bring sports kit, racquets, swimming kit etc. Boarders, aside from what you’d expect to bring, please also bring a towel, and a plug adaptor may be useful.
How many Mid-IB subject courses can I book?
It is possible to book a maximum of two courses. One subject can be studied in the first three-day course. A second subject can be studied in the second three-day course. Alternatively you can choose to come for just one of the courses to study one subject.
Are all the subject choices guaranteed to run?
While we expect to run all the courses offered, the courses can only run if there is sufficient demand and we will notify students and parents as soon as possible if it looks likely that a course will not run after all. In which case switching subject or a full refund of course fees will be offered.
Can I attend the Pre-IB Maths course twice?
The Pre-IB Maths course syllabus covers the same topics on both three-day sessions.
How do I pay for the course?
As you complete the registration form on the application platform, you will be navigate to a payment details page to complete payment of course fees.
What happens if I need to cancel?
Please check the Terms & Conditions for your course.
Do I need insurance?
Students will be responsible for their own medical insurance cover and are urged to take out insurance which fully covers them for damage or loss of their personal belongings for the entire duration of the course, including fees in the event of cancellation after the final payment date.
What time can I arrive at the boarding house?
The boarding staff will expect you to arrive between 16:00 and 19:00 the day before your lessons start.
Does the school organise transport to and from the airport or station?
The school does not organise transport.
Can the school recommend a taxi company?
The school’s boarding community often use the local taxi firm, Beeline: 01732 456214.
Where should I ask the taxi to go to?
Girls will board in Park Grange (postcode TN13 1HY). Boys will board in Aisher House (postcode TN13 1PF).
Where should I book the taxi to pick me up on the last day?
Ask the taxi to pick you up from Duke’s Meadow, which is the big car park near the Sennocke Centre, Sevenoaks School’s sports centre.

Admissions Scholarships
Drama Scholarships
Drama scholarships are offered at Year 9 (13+) and Year 12 (16+). Scholars have the chance to be involved in several productions, performances and workshop style clubs throughout their time at Sevenoaks to help foster a deeper love for theatre and to expand their technical skills on stage or behind the scenes.

Co-curricular Drama
The Drama department is a major contributor to the co-curricular life of the school. Around five productions are performed each year in the Sackville Theatre by the Sevenoaks School Theatre Company (SSTC). The department also runs a variety of clubs for scholars and interested students.
Assessment Process
Drama scholarships are open to candidates from any school. The scholarship assessment will take the form of three tasks which will need preparation in advance: a solo performance, a short presentation, and leading part of a creative workshop as part of a group.
The scholarship is awarded for exhibiting strong theatre-making skills, performance skills, and most importantly co-curricular endeavour. At 13+, candidates would be expected to study Drama through the Middle School. In the Sixth Form candidates are not required to study Theatre as part of their IB Diploma, but it would be advantageous to study Theatre (in Group 6) or English Literature and Performance (in Group 1).
All scholarships are reviewed annually and their continuance is dependent upon satisfactory conduct, attitude, participation and progress. At such a review, holders of awards are expected to assess their own contribution and to set targets for themselves.
Holders of the scholarship will become artistic ambassadors – the best example of what a student of Drama can be – and participate fully in the co-curricular theatre programme.
How to apply
For Year 9 (13+), all candidates who have already been offered and have accepted a place at the school will be invited to apply for a Drama scholarship. This invitation is also extended to current students who joined the school at Year 7 (11+). Drama scholarship applications should be submitted by 1 February of Year 8 and the scholarship assessment day will be held in May.
Year 12 (16+) candidates should apply for a Drama scholarship at the confirmation stage of application. Selected candidates are invited for assessment in November after sitting the academic entrance exams in October. Internal students can be nominated for an honorary scholarship in Year 11.

Music Scholarships
Music scholarships are offered at Year 7 (11+), Year 9 (13+) and Year 12 (16+). What we are looking for, above all, is an enthusiasm for making music.
Holders of awards are expected to meet the normal academic requirements of the school and to be good ambassadors for the Music department. In particular, we are looking for students who will thrive in our creative and stimulating environment. We believe in giving students a significant degree of autonomy in their own learning. We therefore encourage all our students to use their self-motivation and imagination in their musical journey, to deepen their understanding and engagement with music, and to find opportunities of using it as a means of enriching their own lives and the life of the wider community.
Sevenoaks School has a long and proud tradition of music making. All students are encouraged to maximise their experience of music through the wide range of opportunities that the department nurtures inside the busy school framework and which encompasses classical, jazz and popular styles as well as the original creations of the students themselves. A commitment to the opportunities thus created should go without saying. Students who are less willing to embrace this wide variety of opportunities should evaluate whether holding a music scholarship is in their best interests.

Assessment Criteria
At 11+
At 11+ entry, approximately Grade 4 to 5 is required, depending on the instrument the candidate is presenting.
Accurate assessment of a candidate’s musical ability and potential at this young age is difficult. Scholarships may be awarded, however it is likely that we may not be able to make awards to all candidates who are clearly promising, but on whom it is difficult to make a judgement at this time. Children who are unsuccessful at 11+ often make enormous progress in Years 7 and 8. They may choose to re-audition for a scholarship prior to joining Year 9 (13+) after they and their families have met with the Director of Music to discuss their progress in the Lower School.
At 11+ entry we are looking for potential rather than achievement and a genuine enthusiasm for music.
At 13+
At 13+ approximately Grade 6 standard is required depending on the instrument the candidate is presenting. We are looking for potential rather than achievement and a genuine enthusiasm for music.
At 16+
We expect a Sixth Form entrant to be around Grade 8 standard on their principal instrument, although they may not have taken an examination.

Assessment Process
The first stage of the scholarship process involves all applicants making a video recording of themselves performing one piece of music of their choice.
All awards are reviewed annually and their continuance is dependent upon satisfactory conduct, attitude and progress. At the review, holders of awards are expected to assess their own contribution and to set targets for themselves. Scholars will be awarded free instrumental tuition in one instrument.
A satisfactory performance in the appropriate entrance examination is a condition of a Music scholarship.
How to apply

For Year 9 (13+), all candidates who have already been offered and have accepted a place at the school will be invited to apply for a Music scholarship. Music scholarship applications should be submitted by 1 February of Year 8 and the scholarship assessment day will be held in May.
Year 12 (16+) candidates should express an interest in a Music scholarship at the confirmation stage of application. Selected candidates are invited for assessment in November after sitting the academic entrance exams in October.

Choirs, Orchestras and Ensembles
At Sevenoaks, we encourage all student musicians to reach their fullest potential as individual practitioners of their discipline. Complementing this is a wide range of ensemble activities where students play together and work collaboratively on large and small projects throughout their study with us.
Music at Sevenoaks
Choirs, Orchestras and Ensembles
Our ensembles
Choirs
There is a strong choral tradition at Sevenoaks. In addition to the larger groups, such as Choral Society and Chorus, there are also smaller choirs which encourage students to develop their choral singing in a more intimate environment. Most choirs happen in times where they are a school priority, allowing student to attend without clashing with another activity.
All Year 7 pupils participate in choral singing once a week at the beginning of the year and perform in concerts at the end of the Michaelmas term. Thereafter, they can join the Lower School Singers. Styles of music recently covered include musical theatre, Motown, and other well-loved tunes.
The Junior School Chamber Choir comprises of students in Years 8 and 9. This choir is a small group which focuses on folk songs and classical music, thereby allowing younger pupils a taste of choral singing.
The Sevenoaks Chorus is an ensemble in which students can explore the popular music of today, with recent repertoire including movie soundtracks and music by Billie Eilish. Anyone is welcome to join this friendly and relaxed group of singers, who perform at several concerts throughout the year.
The Senior Girls Ensemble is a small group of Sixth Form singers, who are challenged with close harmony singing both accompanied and acapella, which is invaluable in developing skills of listening and intonation.
Sennocke Consort is the senior chamber choir in the school. It is open by invitation to older students, and focuses on classical chamber singing, both accompanied and a cappella. It provides a constructive and supportive environment, especially to students who may wish to apply for choral scholarships at university. In addition to performing regularly in school concerts, the choir sings outside the school environment too, recently performing evensongs in London and Cambridge.
Choral Society is the school’s largest choir. Comprising some 100 students and several keen staff members, the choir specialises in classical music and develops large-scale choral singing in a supportive environment. Choral Society typically works through the year towards a concert in the Lent term, and recent repertoire includes Carl Orff’s Carmina Burana, Dvořák’s Stabat Mater and Haydn’s Nelson Mass.
The Parents and Friends’ Choir is open to any parent of the school as well as to OS, staff and keen friends of Sevenoaks School. This way, our whole school community can join the Choral Society for their Lent term performance and sing a large choral work alongside the students. In addition to this, the choir organises a soiree every summer and supports the work of the Music department throughout the year.
Orchestras
There are two main orchestras at Sevenoaks: the Foundation Orchestra and the Symphony Orchestra.
The Foundation Orchestra is for Years 7-9, and all students who play an orchestral instrument are encouraged to join. This enables them to all learn from each other, as well as develop individually.
The Symphony Orchestra is the more senior orchestra in the school and provides a hugely rewarding environment for students to hone their orchestral skills.
Additional groups include Sevenoaks Strings and the Sevenoaks School Wind Band. These are smaller ensemble groups for string and wind instruments respectively and are aimed primarily at Middle School students.
Chamber Music
Opportunities for playing in small groups is a vital part of our provision for keen musicians.
There are opportunities for pupils to perform in saxophone quartets, piano trios, rock bands, flute choirs and indeed any combination of enthusiastic students.
Chamber music is something we enthusiastically champion and is especially strong at Sevenoaks School. We are regular finalists in Pro Corda’s annual chamber music festival for schools and have been category winners at all levels in recent years.
Sevenoaks School runs regularly over 50 chamber groups which perform in all styles of music from contemporary rock to classical quartet. Rehearsal takes place mainly in the Michaelmas and Lent terms.
Jazz and popular music
The Big Band runs every Thursday after school and attracts the highest calibre of jazz musicians from across the school.
The band plays exciting and challenging repertoire, ranging from swing classics to contemporary compositions to arrangements of Disney songs.
The Big Band is the highlight of major concerts across the school year, including the annual Crash into Christmas concert, which is always a great success with students, staff and parents. The group also invites guest professionals to perform with them, with musicians such as Sonny Rollins, Simon Bates and Harry the Piano having visited the school.
Lower down the school there is a Big Band for Middle School students and, where there are enough takers, a Lower School Jazz Band as well. Brass and saxophone quartets regularly feature in our concerts.
Popular music, songwriting and musical theatre
Many students set up gigs and popular concerts, which also raise money for charities, and these are very well supported. There are competitive performances (based on the popular X Factor TV show), nights which feature specific musical styles, and boarding house concert nights.
Beats and tracks and songwriters’ club are groups that meet to encourage the creation of popular music.
Music often accompanies productions staged by the Drama department and there is an after-school club dedicated to music theatre.
Avant-garde and everything else!
The musical experience at Sevenoaks School is not limited to mainstream genres and groups. Many other projects coexist alongside these.
There is a contemporary music making group called The Space Collective which studies and performs avant-garde and other modern styles.
We are confident that, if a student is suitably interested, we can find and establish a time for that interest to be developed.
“I love singing in the school choirs because it is an amazing opportunity to meet people with similar interests and it expands my knowledge. I love the sound we create and the bonds we form. The conductors are amazing and help me improve a lot!”

Service and Partnerships
Institute of Service and Partnerships
The ethos of Service and Partnerships is central to the Sevenoaks education as we strive to be true to the aims of our Founder, William Sevenoke, and benefit the community. The mission of the Institute of Service and Partnerships (ISP) is to create positive, inclusive, and sustainable social change, incorporating service as a central pillar of a Sevenoaks education.
AIM Kent Partnership
Institute of Service and Partnerships
ISP Publications
Service at Sevenoaks
Secondary partnerships
School Partnerships Alliance
How we work
Working in partnership with other schools, teachers, students, and the community, the ISP helps advance educational innovation and opportunity, and nurture socially engaged young citizens to create a fairer global society.
Our principles:
The ISP has four core strands:
Environmental Sustainability
Equity, Diversity and Inclusion
Educational Partnerships
Student-Led Projects
Service in the curriculum
Students across the school receive service education within the curriculum.
Students learn about Society and Change in weekly lessons.
Students are given an opportunity to work as part of a team to design a Social Entrepreneurship Project.
Students undertake an Advocacy Project in Core Critical Thinking.
Students undertake Thursday afternoon Service activities, alongside Core Critical Thinking and Theory of Knowledge.
Service in the co-curriculum
Outside of the classroom, many students also offer their own time and energy to wider ISP initiatives such as the Eco Committee, Junior Eco Club, Education Society, EDI Action Committee, organising themed weeks and other events each year.
Partnerships
We have a wide range of local and global partnerships helping communities in and around Sevenoaks as well as internationally.
A significant number of our students work collaboratively to organise their own community projects to raise funds for and awareness of local and international charities.
Locally, we have close partnerships with primary schools through the Sevenoaks Partnership of Primary Schools, and with secondary schools through the Kent Academies Network and Knole Academy.
Globally, we engage in partnerships to promote sustainable development and cultural understanding.
Students provide regular weekly support as well as fundraising for community-led projects. We also operate annual educational trips to countries where we have partnerships, including Morocco and South Africa.
Students in service groups collaborate with organisations like EduSpots, supporting community-led education spaces and deliver STEM and literacy programs. Students also work with local artists, participate in conservation efforts, and raise funds for Education for All in Morocco. Through these global programs, Sevenoaks School aims to foster global citizenship, promote education, and address issues such as poverty, gender inequality, and conservation.
“Thanks to a brilliant Gen Z project we ran with inspiring and exceptionally bright Year 11 Sevenoaks School pupils, we’ve been fortunate to have their support ever since and we couldn’t be more grateful. Their enthusiasm, generosity, and commitment to helping the children we support at Dreams Come True has been genuinely heartwarming. A huge thank you to every student involved, and a special shout-out to our wonderful in school Dream Champion Kathy O’Donnell whose passion and leadership have made this partnership flourish. ”
“Please pass on my thanks to all involved in the organisation of the Chess Tournament on Wednesday afternoon - it was a super event that all the pupils from Fordcombe enjoyed taking part in. Many thanks for all the support that Sevenoaks school gives to local primary schools - what you do is very special.”
“My sincerest gratitude to the students at Sevenoaks School. Their positive attitude has supported Oak Class to fully engage in a range of outstanding coding lessons. These sessions have clearly taken time and effort to plan and resource. To see the joy on the pupils' faces makes it so worthwhile. ”

Since September 2023, we have been working in partnership with AIM Kent, an organisation that runs weekly 11+ preparation courses at Sevenoaks during term time, as well as holiday sessions and mock 11+ exams.
The 11+ preparation classes are free to attend and are targeted towards children from low-income families. They seek to boost confidence, break down barriers to grammar school entry and promote social mobility. AIM’s vision fully aligns with our core objective of advancing educational opportunity for all those in our local community.

service in the co-curriculum

Participating in Service enables students to develop transferable skills that will be key to success after their time at Sevenoaks, such as decision-making, teamwork, adaptability and initiative. The service group activities on a Thursday are largely student-led.

Fusion magazine
Sevenoaks students share their passion for science with younger audiences by participating in the Fusion magazine service group. In the process, students strengthen their creativity, teamwork, collaboration, and leadership skills.
During STEM Week, local primary pupils are invited to submit their science questions, with selected entries featured in Fusion.
